thread:
Sam: quick follow-up on the continuous-batcher refactor RFC — thinking out loud about a thin "deadline shim" that can attach soft deadlines to leases so downstream queues can preempt without full global coordination. want to sync on tradeoffs.
Maria: thin shim sounds promising. curious how we encode origin/priority so it survives enqueue/requeue cycles.
Lee: +1. main concern: metadata bloat per-request. we already track sequence length + kv-hint; adding a few fields increases memory pressure in hot paths.
Zane: can we encode as a single bitfield int and keep it atomic? e.g., 8 bits for origin, 8 bits for deadline-tier, 8 bits for preempt-hint.
Sam: idea: bitfield for fast-path admission checks, and a separate sidecar map for verbose debug info only used by observability / traces. cheap in steady state.
Avi: how do we prevent lease re-handed to a different lane from losing deadline semantics? requeue -> different host -> different scheduler instance.
Maria: propagate the lease token with the bitfield baked in. token format: <lease-id>:<bitfield>. on re-enqueue, scheduler extracts bitfield and retains it.
Lee: code sketch:
```
// lease token layout
struct Token { u64 lease_id; u32 attrs; }
// attrs layout: [origin:8][tier:8][preempt:8][reserved:8]
```
Sam: thanks. runtime perf question: do we decode attrs on every enqueue/dequeue? or only at admission checks? ideally only at admission and preempt fast-path; avoid per-message decode in hot loops.
Zane: admission needs it. other ops can pass token opaque. also consider using memcmp-friendly layout so no endian work on x86.
Maria: tradeoff: If we only decode at admission, we risk stale attrs if policy updates mid-flight. e.g., origin weight changes -> we might over-admit.
Avi: can we attach a policy-version to the token so admission can compare and, if stale, consult central policy and stamp new attrs? cheap optimistic path.
Lee: that implies additional RPCs on miss. prefer local policy cache with TTL and a fast reload path.
Sam: observability: we need to surface enqueue/requeue events with attrs so SRE can reason about tail latency regressions. suggested span tags: lease_id, attrs, policy_version, enqueue_ts.
Maria: agrees. also add a small counter metric: "requeue_due_to_preempt" with labels (lane, origin).
Zane: another corner: multi-tenant headroom. if we let leases carry a "soft-deadline" tier that triggers admission bump, we must ensure it doesn't let tenants consume others' headroom. need per-tenant credits on accept.
Avi: per-tenant credits + per-lane caps. admission checks both. if "soft-deadline" tries to bump, it must atomically reserve credit or fail.
Sam: atomic reservation across lanes is hard. propose: try-local-reserve, if fail, fallback to global-queue fallback (best-effort lower perf). document as graceful degrade.
Lee: sounds reasonable. log-level: warn on fallback occurrences so we can track.
Maria: long-term: consider moving from token-carrying attrs to a tiny distributed lease registry (Raft-ish) for heavy-weight semantics (strict deadlines). for now token approach covers 95% cheap cases.
Zane: agree. registry would add complexity but give strong correctness for strict SLO tenants.
Avi: one more: what about admission tests for function-calling/streaming requests where token geometry is different? need to ensure attrs survive fragmenting.
Sam: for streaming, keep attrs on the stream root token and propagate fragment IDs that reference it. fragments remain lightweight.
Maria: next steps: Sam/Lee to prototype token bitfield encoding + local policy cache. Zane to add metrics/trace tags. Avi to write the acceptance criteria for per-tenant credit fallback.
Sam: can we aim for a short spike this sprint (2d) + demo in eng-runtime sync? @deploy-bot can you create a PR draft template for the spike branch?
deploy-bot: created ticket INF-6421 with checklist: prototype bitfield token, local policy cache, metrics, stream tests. assigned Sam, Lee, Zane, Avi. ETA 2026-03-28.
Sam: awesome — thanks. posting this summary to the RFC thread after the spike.
Maria: thanks all. :thumbsup:
